Amusement route location calculator · guide

How much commission to pay a location for arcade machines

Commission splits on a coin-op route are usually set once, by habit, and never looked at again. But what a location can afford to be paid depends on what its machines take, how often you visit and how far you drive. The same 50 percent can be a good deal at one stop and a loss at another.

The method

For each location, take the monthly gross, then subtract prizes, card fees, repairs, licences, machine wear and driving. Divide what remains, after the commission, by the hours the stop takes. That is profit per route hour. Set it equal to the hourly you want and solve for the commission: that is the most you can pay.

Example assumptions: a target of $35 an hour, $0.60 per mile, prizes at 8% of takings, 40% of takings by card at 3.5%, $18 a month repairs and $120 a year licence per machine, machines costing $3,500 over 7 years.

A five-location route

LocationTake / machine / weekProfit / hourHighest commission
Corner bar (pool tables)$140.00$10366.9%
Bowling alley (arcade)$85.00$12560.3%
Laundromat (claw machine)$210.00$15872.1%
Truck stop (three games)$60.00-$539.6%
Pizza parlour (kiddie rides)$40.00-$1338.5%

The route averages $88 an hour, which hides the fact that 2 of the five locations lose money before paying you. The truck stop pays its owner 55 percent and sits 70 miles away; the pizza parlour's rides take too little to carry a visit. The route looks healthy only because the bowling alley and laundromat carry it.

Try your own numbers in the calculator. It also shows the weekly take each location needs.

Common questions

What is a fair commission split for amusement machines?

There is no single fair split. Splits of 40 to 60 percent are common, but the right one for a given location is the highest commission that still earns you your target hourly, which depends on take, visits and miles. The worked example below shows how far apart those ceilings can be.

Why do some locations lose money even when they pay?

Because a visit costs the same whether the machines took much or little: the drive, the time on site, and per-machine repairs and licences. A low take spread over those fixed costs can go negative once the commission comes off.

When should I pull machines from a location?

When even a zero commission cannot reach your target hourly at the current take, visits and miles. Otherwise the calculator gives the commission to ask for.

AMUSEMENT ROUTE LOCATION CALCULATOR · RUNS IN YOUR BROWSER · NOTHING UPLOADED

Is each location on your arcade, pool table or claw machine route worth the drive?

Type each location's take, commission, visits and miles. The tool takes out commission, prizes, card fees, repairs, licences, machine wear and driving, shows what each stop earns per route hour, the weekly take it needs, and the highest commission you can pay and still earn your target.

The method with a worked example: how much commission to pay a location for arcade machines.

How it is built

Gross: weekly take per machine times machines times 52 over 12. Commission is a percentage of that gross. Prizes are a percentage of takings. Card fees are the card share of takings times the fee. Repairs, licence and machine wear (price over life) are charged per machine; driving is visits times round-trip miles times your cost per mile.

Hours are visits per month times minutes per visit. Profit is before paying yourself or your tax; profit per hour is compared with your target. Take needed and highest commission are exact: the test suite recomputes the location at each and checks it earns your target to the cent.

Common questions

How much commission should I pay a location for arcade or pool table machines?

As much as still leaves you your target hourly after prizes, card fees, repairs, licences, machine wear and driving. That ceiling differs by location because it depends on the take, the visits and the miles. This calculator solves for it location by location.

How do I know if a route location is worth keeping?

Compare profit per route hour with the hourly you want to take home. Profit here is the take less commission, prizes, card fees, repairs, licences, machine wear and driving; hours are the visits times the minutes each one takes, driving included. A location below your target is either a commission to renegotiate or a stop to drop.

What weekly take does a machine need to be worth placing?

The calculator shows the break-even weekly take per machine for each location: the take at which the location earns exactly your target hourly at its current commission, visits and miles. Compare it with what the machines really collect.

Does driving time count against a route location?

Yes. A distant stop with a small take can lose money in fuel and spend hours on the road. Enter the round-trip miles and the minutes per visit including the drive, and the tool charges both.

Is my route data uploaded?

No. Everything runs in your browser, there are no accounts, and nothing is sent to a server. Use Save to download a scenario file.

Is this business or tax advice?

No. It is arithmetic on the numbers you type. Licensing, location agreements and tax depend on where you operate; check with an accountant or your state or local licensing office.
